name: 驛麺 らぁ～めん京 山陽姫路駅店 (Ekimen Ramen Kyo Sanyo-Himeji Station)
neighborhood: 山陽姫路駅構内 (Inside Sanyo-Himeji Station)
notes: Part of the ラーメン京（みやこ）chain headquartered in Kyoto, with multiple outlets across Hyogo, Kyoto, Nara, and Shiga prefectures. The Sanyo-Himeji station branch operates on the 2nd floor directly beside the ticket gates, catering to commuters seeking a fast, inexpensive bowl.

name: 東来春 (Tonraishun)
notes: [Mom & Pop] Founded in 1946 (Showa 21) in postwar Himeji as an udon and fried-rice shop. During the era of food shortages, the practice of using scraps left over from cooking—such as pork fat trimmings and cabbage cores—without waste in staff meals is said to be the origin of its shumai.
